title: Hezbollah Launches 105-Wave Attack on Israel — Most Intense Single Day of Conflict; 1 Killed in Nahariya, 14 Injured; Drone Hits IDF Zone in S. Lebanon — Day 87
detail: The Alma Center reported 105 Hezbollah attack waves launched against Israel on May 25, 2026 (Day 87) — the highest single-day total since the conflict began February 28 and the most intense barrage since the Lebanon front opened March 2. Cumulative Hezbollah attack waves since the start of the conflict now stand at 1,084+. Rockets struck the city of Nahariya in northern Israel, killing at least one man and injuring 14 others — the most significant Israeli civilian toll from a single Hezbollah attack in weeks. A drone also struck an area where IDF troops were operating in southern Lebanon, though no Israeli casualties were reported from that incident. The massive barrage continued despite the 45-day Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extension announced May 16, which nominally requires Hezbollah disarmament and IDF withdrawal from occupied southern Lebanese positions — neither of which has occurred. The escalation on Day 87 arrives as the broader US-Iran nuclear deal negotiations are at their most advanced stage yet, suggesting Hezbollah may be attempting to strengthen Iran's hand before any final framework is signed or to pre-position for the post-deal period. Iron Dome and David's Sling systems were activated extensively along the northern front.

media.caption: Day 87: Hezbollah launches record 105 attack waves against Israel — 1 killed in Nahariya, 14 injured; most intense single day of conflict

title: Rubio: 'Pretty Solid Thing on the Table' — US-Iran MoU Framework Provides 60-Day Window to Finalize; Nuclear Enrichment Details NOT Included in Initial MoU — Day 87
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on May 25, 2026 (Day 87) confirmed there is 'a pretty solid thing on the table' in the US-Iran negotiations — a notably more definitive characterization than his May 24 'significant progress' language. Rubio clarified that negotiations are 'still a work in progress' but that the framework being discussed would commit Iran to never possessing a nuclear weapon and to surrendering its highly enriched uranium stockpile. The emerging MoU structure, per CNN's May 25 live reporting, would provide parties 60 days to reach final deal points, rather than constituting a comprehensive final agreement — meaning the MoU would not itself resolve all issues but would create a structured negotiating window under a ceasefire. Critically, nuclear enrichment details — the most divisive issue between Washington and Tehran — are NOT included in the initial MoU text, to be addressed in the 60-day follow-on negotiation. Former CIA Director David Petraeus said on CNBC on Day 87 that Iran is 'in the process of blinking' over the Strait of Hormuz, citing Iran's restoration of access to 30 of its 33 missile sites along the strait as evidence of Iranian concessions — though Iran continued to frame the moves as 'navigational service fee' structures rather than free passage. Oil prices continued to fall on Day 87 deal momentum: CNN described prices as 'plunging' as the US and Iran edge closer. Rubio's evolution — from 'slight progress' (Day 84) to 'significant progress' (Day 86) to 'pretty solid thing on the table' (Day 87) — represents the most positive US diplomatic language since the conflict began.

media.caption: Day 87: Rubio says 'pretty solid thing on the table' — US-Iran MoU framework provides 60-day window to finalize; nuclear enrichment NOT in initial MoU

title: Bank of Israel Cuts Rates 25bps to 3.75% — Cites Iran War Deal Progress; Shekel Surges to 30+ Year High (~2.9 NIS/Dollar) — Day 87
detail: The Bank of Israel cut its benchmark interest rate from 4.00% to 3.75% (a 25 basis point reduction) on May 25, 2026 (Day 87) — the second rate cut of 2026. The Monetary Policy Committee explicitly cited progress toward an end to the Iran war as a key factor in its decision, pointing to the surging shekel as evidence that markets are pricing in a high probability of deal closure. The Israeli shekel appreciated to approximately 2.9 NIS per US dollar — a 30+ year high — on compounding deal optimism from Trump's 'largely negotiated' claim (Day 85), Axios's nuclear deal parameters (Day 86), and Rubio's 'pretty solid thing on the table' (Day 87). The Bank of Israel rate cut serves as a significant institutional confidence signal — it reflects the Israeli central bank's assessment that the security risk premium on the Israeli economy is declining materially. Israeli opposition chairman Yair Golan (Democrats party) publicly criticized PM Netanyahu on Day 87, stating that 'the arrangements most critical to Israel's security are being finalized without us' and that Israel will 'likely learn the details of the agreement only after the fact' — reflecting deep Israeli political tension over being excluded from the US-Iran deal framework. The Bank of Israel's 25bps cut marks the first time in the conflict that Israeli monetary policy has moved to reflect war resolution rather than war escalation.

media.caption: Day 87: Bank of Israel cuts rates 25bps to 3.75% citing Iran deal progress; shekel hits 30+ year high at ~2.9 NIS/USD

title: US Intelligence: Iran Retained ~70% Missile Stockpile, Restored 30 of 33 Hormuz Missile Sites, Drone Production Restarted — Full Reconstitution in 6 Months, Not Years — Day 87
detail: US intelligence assessments confirmed on May 25, 2026 (Day 87) that Iran's military reconstitution has exceeded all prior IC timelines. Key intelligence findings: Iran has retained approximately 70% of its pre-war missile stockpile despite 87 days of US-Israeli strikes; Iran still controls approximately 70% of its mobile missile launchers; Iran has restored access to 30 of its 33 missile sites positioned along the Strait of Hormuz; drone production has already restarted at multiple facilities; and full military reconstitution — including restoring destroyed fixed facilities — is now estimated at 6 months, not the years previously projected. The intelligence summary, described by sources cited in multiple outlets, reveals that Operation Epic Fury's objective of permanently degrading Iran's military-industrial base has fallen significantly short of its stated goals. The missile reconstitution intelligence creates a dual-pressure dynamic: it provides an argument for urgency in concluding a nuclear deal (Iran is rebuilding faster than expected, reducing US leverage), while also energizing critics — including from the Israeli side — who argue the deal should require permanent dismantlement rather than a moratorium. Former CIA Director David Petraeus, in his May 25 CNBC interview, appeared to reference this intelligence when noting Iran had restored 30 of 33 missile sites on the Strait while also characterizing Iran as 'blinking' — suggesting the US intelligence community views Iran's strategic posture as weakened but its operational resilience as stronger than anticipated. The 6-month reconstitution timeline gives negotiators a concrete deadline by which the leverage of the current military situation will be substantially eroded.

media.caption: Day 87: US intel confirms Iran retained ~70% missile stockpile, restored 30 of 33 Hormuz sites, drone production restarted — full reconstitution in 6 months
